issues.title: AI moves into engineering software, excavators drive themselves
issues.summary: Nemetschek put an AI layer into Allplan, SCIA, FRILO, Archicad and Bluebeam, including connectors for outside AI assistants. Bedrock Robotics raised $600M for self-driving excavators, and a Swedish start-up was selected for EU money to make cement from industrial residues in Latvia. In Switzerland, the new Sisikon tunnel is blasted with a nitrate-free explosive so its rock can go into Lake Uri. Our focus: the basic idea of circular construction.

issues.title: AI agents arrive in the site office, but where is the value?
issues.summary: Procore turned AI agents loose on submittals and procurement logs, and EarthCam plugged its jobsite cameras straight into ChatGPT and Claude. At the same time, two surveys show that most builders still struggle to measure what AI actually brings. In materials, Holcim recycled a third more demolition waste, a Zurich start-up sold its first carbon credits for timber buildings, and data centres may become the first big buyers of low-carbon concrete. Our focus: how large language models work, in plain terms.
issues.focus_title: How large language models work, in plain terms

issues.title: Robots get funded, geotech meets live data, concrete goes round
issues.summary: Construction robotics drew big money this week: ICON's multi-storey 3D printer, Origin's wall-finishing robot and All3's legged site robots. Hexagon is buying the geotechnical software maker Rocscience to feed live sensor data into engineering models, a Dutch start-up got €100M to recycle demolition concrete into new concrete, and a new EU project wants reclaimed building parts to get a 'beautiful' second life. Our focus: what BIM really is, and why it is not yet a digital twin.
issues.focus_title: BIM is not a digital twin (yet)
